newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Kuwait naphtha term talks seen finalised Feb 27.
newsitem.headline: Kuwait naphtha term talks seen finalised Feb 27.

text.p: Talks between Asian buyers and supplier Kuwait Petroleum Corp (KPC) over the supply of two million tonnes of full-range naphtha were expected to be completed by Thursday, traders said on Tuesday.
They said the first round of talks, where buyers submit bids, concluded on Tuesday and the second round, where the final premium is agreed upon, will be concluded Thursday.
But traders said one buyer may have already concluded a renewal of its contract with KPC at between $13 and $14 per tonne premium over Mideast naphtha spot quotes on a free-on-board basis.
Other buyers were likely to follow and conclude their contracts for lifting March 1997 to February 1998 within that range, traders said.
This would set a much higher premium than KPC's last round of talks for August 1996-September 1997, which were settled at $7.90 premium.
